About the Position

The University of Glasgow is offering Sanctuary PhD Scholarships for PhD applicants with Refugee or Asylum Seeker status. Open to prospective PhD students in the College of Arts and Humanities commencing in October 2026. Provides 100% tuition fee waiver and a £5,000 per year stipend. Deadline: 29 May 2026.

OpportunityCollege of Arts and Humanities Sanctuary PhD Scholarship at the University of Glasgow
HostUniversity of Glasgow
LocationGlasgow, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingFully Funded
Stipend£5,000/year
Application Deadline29 May 2026
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Funding detail: 100% tuition fee waiver (Home/RUK fees only) plus £5,000 per annum stipend towards study costs

College of Arts and Humanities Sanctuary PhD Scholarship Overview

The University of Glasgow is offering 4 Sanctuary PhD Scholarships (1 per College) for PhD applicants to the University, with Refugee or Asylum Seeker status[reference:0]. This scholarship is open to prospective PhD students in the College of Arts and Humanities at the University of Glasgow applying for commencing their PhDs in October 2026[reference:1].

Scholarship Value

The scholarship will meet the cost of tuition fees for the minimum duration of your programme. The College of Arts and Humanities Sanctuary PhD Scholarship also provides a £5,000 per year stipend, to assist with study costs[reference:2].

Number of Scholarships

1 per College (4 total across the University).

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants must:

  • currently be located in the United Kingdom and be eligible for Home or Rest of UK (RUK) fee status;
  • recipients must be able to be based within commutable distance to the UofG Campus at which they will be registered. This Scholarship cannot be awarded to undertake a PhD by Distance;
  • have lodged an application to a PhD programme within the College of Arts and Humanities
  • note that only PhD programmes are eligible - other Doctorate or Research Masters programmes are not eligible.
  • note that only full-time study is eligible – applications for part-time study cannot be considered.

AND

  • have submitted a claim for Asylum in the UK OR are actively appealing a negative decision on a claim for asylum in the UK OR have been granted Refugee Status, Humanitarian Protection (HP) or Discretionary Leave (DL) by the Home Office, as a result of an asylum claim
  • OR have come to the United Kingdom through schemes such as: UK Resettlement Scheme (UKRS), Afghan citizens Resettlement Scheme, Afghan Relocations and Assistance Policy (ARAP), Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme (VPRS), Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme (Homes for Ukraine), Ukraine Family Scheme[reference:3].

Assessment Criteria

  • The College of Arts and Humanities expects all funded PhD candidates to be able to complete their PhD within the funded period.
  • Applications will be judged in terms of qualifications, preparedness to undertake a PhD, and the quality of the proposed project.
  • All applications are reviewed and decided by a College funding panel[reference:4].

How to Apply

In order to be considered for this scholarship you must:

  1. Apply for a PhD within the College of Arts and Humanities as soon as possible, and no later than 29 May 2026.
  2. Please indicate in the funding section of your admission application that you will be applying for the 'Sanctuary PhD Scholarship'.
  3. Note if you have any issues with evidencing that you meet the entry requirements of the PhD Programme, please contact the Displaced and Conflict Affected (DACA) team in Admissions via their online enquiry form as soon as possible, making sure you select 'I have been affected by forced displacement and conflict' as the reason for the enquiry.
  4. All applicants must also complete the CoAH Sanctuary PhD Scholarship application via the Scholarships Application Portal. The scholarship is under 'College of Arts & Humanities Postgraduate Research Scholarships > COAH-26-004'.
  5. As part of the Scholarships Application process, you will need to upload the following documents: CoAH Sanctuary Scholarship Application Form, CoAH Sanctuary Scholarship Supervisor Statement, and Demographic eligibility documentation.

Demographic Eligibility Documentation

Applications CANNOT be considered without the relevant Demographic eligibility documentation to support them:

If you are subject to Home Office Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting, please provide your:

  • Application Registration Card (ARC) - Front AND Back
  • Immigration Bail Reporting Notice (this may also be referred to as a Temporary Admission Document or BAIL 201) - please include every page of this document

OR

If you are not subject to Home Office Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting, please provide your:

  • Application Registration Card (ARC) - Front AND Back
  • The most recent documentation you have received from the Home Office in conjunction with your application/appeal - this should show your Home Office reference number.

OR

  • A share code provided by the UK government that can prove your right to study in the UK. You will have access to a share code if you have an e-visa[reference:5].

Additional Support

Prospective PhD applicants who are in need of urgent help to escape from discrimination, persecution, violence or conflict, may also wish to explore opportunities and support available via the Council for At-Risk Academics (CARA), of which the University of Glasgow is a member institution[reference:6].

Contact

For more information about this scholarship, please contact the University of Glasgow Scholarships team.

Closing Date

29 May 2026[reference:7].

Official Link

https://www.gla.ac.uk/scholarships/collegeofartsandhumanitiessanctuaryphdscholarship/

Important Notes

  • Always confirm the full requirements and current deadline on the official website before applying.
  • Prepare the requested documents early — competitive awards are often decided on complete, on-time submissions.
  • Funding terms shown here reflect the listing at the time of publication and can be updated by the provider.
